issues.title: Holding on

takeaways.t: The FOMC kept rates at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissenters wanting a hike, and Chair Warsh said 2027 will have only seven of eight meetings set rates, shifting to 6 of 8 in 2028.
FedWatch puts a December hike at about 85%, with two more quarter-point increases likely in the first half of 2027; the 10-year yield rose 5 bps to 5.045%.
Search growth fell short of expectations and free cash flow was negative $9.1B, though cloud beat; Microsoft stayed free-cash-flow positive and rose after hours.
Shares jumped 15.15% to $7.07 after Nelson Peltz's fund offered to buy the burger chain for $1.4B.
Q3 profit roughly doubled to $61.3M from $31.9M, with namesake restaurant comparable sales up 15.2% year over year.
Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, starting at $2,899 with an OLED display, on sale Nov. 6.

issues.note: Market numbers are the Wednesday close.

takeaways.t: Stocks edged up as the Fed held rates, with the S&P 500 up 0.28% and Nasdaq up 0.27%, while the 10-year yield rose 5 bps to 5.045% and oil gained 1.39% to $101.29.
The Fed kept rates at 3.75%-4.00% with two of 12 members dissenting for a hike over 3.7% inflation; odds of a December hike are around 85%.
Prediction markets brought in $173M last quarter, more than six times a year ago, helping record revenue of $1.42B (+12%), but EPS missed and shares fell 3.30%.
Prediction markets traded over $14B in notional volume last weekend, a record two-day stretch, with Kalshi alone above $10B and $1.4B already traded on midterm markets.
Vertiv jumped 16.40% and Wendy’s 15.15% on a $1.4B Trian offer, while F5 fell 20.43%, Enphase 16.03% and Boston Scientific 5.84% after a guidance cut.
DoorDash is nearing a roughly $17B deal for Instacart, and the Energy Department is backing Constellation with $5B to upgrade nuclear plants.
Chip and AI hardware enthusiasm lifted the Nasdaq 1.18% and S&P 500 0.60%, while oil slid 1.90% to $99.83 on Middle East de-escalation hopes.
Shares fell over 10% as the 737 Max rate of 47 a month slips to early 2027 (about 42 now); commercial unit lost $697M and Q3 deliveries dropped to 161 from 171.
Free cash flow was $464M versus roughly $325M expected, keeping the $1B-$3B full-year target in reach despite $45.9B of debt.
Q3 sales rose 7% to $13.4B and adjusted EPS rose 11% to 91 cents; volume grew 5% and the full-year outlook was raised, with shares flat.
JetBlue jumped 18.99% on an upbeat outlook, SoFi gained 13.42% and Pentair 12.74%, while Xylem sank 14.26% and Innodata fell 25.32% after about 550 layoffs.
Full-time MBA applications fell 27% for the class of 2028; Harvard's endowment still grew over $11B on a roughly 27% return.
Filed a 318-page prospectus showing $16.3B in H1 revenue vs $1.2B a year earlier; Q3 growth slowed to 45% from 140%, and Wall Street cut its valuation target to $1.5T from $2T.
Added 406,000 postpaid phones (nearly double estimates) and raised its outlook, but a slight revenue miss sent shares down 3.38%.
Reports of a push for 80,000+ US cell sites weigh on carriers; TD Cowen pegs a national network at $80B+, and SpaceX closed a $40B Apollo financing.
EQT agreed to buy Range Resources for ~$12.8B (RRC +17.68%); Surgery Partners jumped 47.62% on a reported ~$6B Bon Secours Mercy bid.
Plans buyouts for roughly 60,000 employees, about 27% of its workforce; shares rose 1.54%.
Tesla +5.21% on a Barclays upgrade; Fair Isaac -13.15% and JetBlue -9.71%; Petrobras -13.99% and Nu -16.95% after Lula's election win.
US crude jumped 4.2% to $103.67 on Middle East fears; gold hit its lowest since July.
Record $20.1B revenue (+9%) and profit up 28% to $3.71B, but stock fell 3.7% on a slight miss and ~3,500 job cuts.
SK Hynix shelved a Solidigm US listing, Firmus scrapped its IPO, and Oura delayed its own.
Reportedly trimmed its funding target to $1.25T from $1.4T on softer demand.
AT&T fell 8% and T-Mobile 7.7% on reports SpaceX is seeking access to 80,000 cell towers.
US luxury spending fell 6% in September while high earners drove most Beige Book districts.
Nasdaq had its worst day since June.
AI spending worries. Stock split in January keeps Zuckerberg's voting control.
Fuel up 68% at American, but premium-cabin revenue is growing 17-23%.
Staples +5%, healthcare at a record, P&G +5.6%, Lockheed +6.9%.
Lam Research -11.8%. Semis had their worst week since April 2025.
